articles.body: Imagine building a modern web application or content platform that showcases thousands of images and video assets. In a local development environment, everything renders smoothly. However, as soon as the application is tested across diverse devices, screen sizes, and network conditions, practical media challenges emerge: High-resolution camera uploads consume several megabytes of bandwidth, leading to poor Core Web Vitals scores and noticeable layout lag on mobile connections. Standard center-cropping abruptly clips human faces or primary product subjects when adapting horizontal 16:9 images into vertical 9:16 mobile formats. Adapting images to new aspect ratios without cropping leaves awkward empty letterboxing unless complex generative fills are manually created.

articles.body: Short answer: Choose OpenAI ChatGPT for dynamic casual dialogue, Claude for explainable complex reasoning, and Gemini when minimal-response latency dominates; keep all three behind one CRM action contract. Choose the chatbot service by the CRM action you must produce, not by which demo sounds most human. For an in-app workflow that turns sales calls into CRM actions, I would start with OpenAI ChatGPT for precise, casual dialogue, choose Claude when reasoning and explainability carry more weight, and evaluate Gemini when minimal-response latency is the primary constraint. Provider portability is the architectural decision that keeps that choice reversible.

articles.body: A post made the rounds on X this week. A developer says OpenAI shut down his account. His story: he was running a log4j decompiler on his own machine, for his own work. The deactivation email called it "Cyber Abuse". We can't verify his story. Take it as his account, not established fact. But watch the reaction. Developers believed it instantly. That reaction is the real news: people already expect their AI tools to turn on them. You're renting your job Check the paperwork. OpenAI's Terms of Use say they "reserve the right to suspend or terminate your access" if they decide you breached their usage policies. Anthropic's consumer terms say the same, and its usage policy adds that a Safeguards Team runs "detection and monitoring" to enforce it. That's their right. It's their service.

articles.title: Current VAT Rate vs Transaction-Date VAT Rate: Why the Difference Matters
articles.excerpt: Current VAT Rate vs Transaction-Date VAT Rate: Why the Difference Matters A VAT rate lookup usually starts with a simple question: What is the VAT rate for this country and product? But there is anoth…
articles.body: Current VAT Rate vs Transaction-Date VAT Rate: Why the Difference Matters A VAT rate lookup usually starts with a simple question: What is the VAT rate for this country and product? But there is another question that matters just as much: For which date? If you are calculating a transaction happening today, the current rate may be exactly what you need. If you are reviewing a transaction from six months ago, processing an old refund, migrating historical orders, or investigating a discrepancy, blindly applying today's rate can give you the wrong answer. That is the difference between a current VAT rate and a transaction-date VAT rate . The numeric percentage may even look familiar. The evidence behind it can be completely different.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 24, 1946: V-2 rocket takes 1st photos of Earth from space
articles.excerpt: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. While these grainy, black-and-white images might not look like much today, they were a huge deal at the time, because no one had ever seen Earth from space before. The V-2 rocket launched from the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. It carried a 35-millimeter motion picture camera that captured a new frame every second and a half. The rocket soared to an altitude of about 65 miles before falling back to Earth. Both the rocket and the camera were destroyed after crashing into the Earth at a speed of about 340 miles per hour. But the film survived because it was protected inside a steel case. Scientists had to drive out into the New Mexico desert to retrieve the film.

The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. articles.title: Medusa's eye, Halloween fireballs and more: 5 skywatching targets to look out for this spooky season
articles.excerpt: Five spooky skywatching targets perfect for naked eye stargazing this Halloween!
articles.body: The spooky season is officially here! To celebrate, we've put together a list of five Halloween-themed skywatching targets that you can enjoy with nothing but the naked eye or binoculars and, of course, clear skies. Over millennia, the night sky has helped shape human beliefs. In return, we have imprinted our myths, stories and perceptions upon it, seeing monsters and mythology in the twinkling lights of the stars and assigning sinister aspects to innocent cosmic objects. Many of these ghostly impressions and meanings have survived to the present day. Here are a few of our favorites. The Pleiades open star cluster Don't be fooled by their beauty; the blue-white stars of the Pleiades are dripping in spooky lore.

Rosetta’s Selfie Explanation: This Rosetta spacecraft selfie was snapped on October 7th, 2014. At the time the comet-chasing spacecraft was about 472 million kilometers from planet Earth, but only 16 kilometers from the surface of comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko .
